title: Bakewell Tart
subtitle: Shortcrust tart with raspberry jam and almond frangipane
excerpt: A shortcrust pastry case spread with raspberry jam and filled with a light, nutty almond frangipane. One of the most popular British teatime bakes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bakewell tart takes its name from the town of Bakewell in Derbyshire, where a confection of pastry, jam, and almond-flavoured filling has been made since at least the nineteenth century. The original Bakewell Pudding is different: it was allegedly created by accident at the White Horse Inn in the 1820s when a cook spread an egg and almond mixture over the jam rather than mixing it into the pastry, and has a runny egg-based filling rather than frangipane. The modern Bakewell Tart with frangipane is a later development and is the version most commonly made at home and sold in bakeries. The Bakewell Pudding is still made in Bakewell itself. The cherry Bakewell, with fondant icing and a glace cherry on top, is a commercial confection with no historical connection to Bakewell and is not made here.

content.text: Blind-bake the pastry case first to prevent a soggy bottom. The frangipane will puff up during baking and settle slightly as it cools; this is normal. The tart is done when the frangipane is set, golden, and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cool completely before slicing: the frangipane needs time to firm up.

Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Roll out the pastry and line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill for 20 minutes. Blind-bake with paper and beans for 15 minutes. Remove the beans and paper and bake for 5 more minutes until pale golden. Cool slightly.
Beat together the soft butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the ground almonds, flour, and almond extract.

Spread the raspberry jam over the base of the tart case. Spoon the frangipane over the jam and smooth gently. Scatter with flaked almonds. Bake at 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4 for 30 to 35 minutes until the frangipane is golden and set. Cool completely before slicing.
